content: Cervical priming is recommended for certain groups of women undergoing first-trimester surgical abortion. Nitric oxide (NO) donors are known to induce cervical ripening without causing uterine contractions. However, their efficacy and associated side effects remain a concern. A systematic review was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness, side effects, and potential for reducing complications when using NO donors for cervical ripening before first-trimester surgical abortion. The review included randomized controlled trials comparing NO donors alone or in combination with other methods. Nine studies involving 766 participants were included in the analysis. No serious complications, such as infections requiring antibiotics, blood transfusions, unintended operations, cervical injuries, uterine perforations, or deaths, were reported in the trials. NO donors were found to be more effective than placebo or no treatment in achieving cervical ripening. Baseline cervical dilation before the procedure was greater in the NO donor group, with a mean difference of 0.30 mm (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.01 to 0.58). However, there was no significant difference in the cumulative force required to dilate the cervix to 8 mm, headache incidence, abdominal pain, or patient satisfaction between the NO donor group and the placebo/no treatment group. Women receiving NO donors experienced more nausea and vomiting, with a risk ratio (RR) of 2.62 (95% CI 1.07 to 6.45). When compared to prostaglandins, NO donors were less effective for cervical ripening. The cumulative force required to dilate the cervix to 8–9 mm was higher in the NO donor group (mean difference 13.12, 95% CI 9.72 to 16.52), and baseline cervical dilation was lower (mean difference -0.73, 95% CI -1.01 to -0.45). However, the likelihood of achieving cervical dilation greater than 8 mm within three hours was higher in the NO donor group (RR 6.67, 95% CI 2.21 to 20.09). Side effects such as headache (RR 5.13, 95% CI 3.29 to 8.00), palpitations (RR 3.43, 95% CI 1.64 to 7.15), dizziness (RR 3.29, 95% CI 1.46 to 7.41), and intraoperative blood loss (mean difference 33.59 mL, 95% CI 24.50 to 42.67) were more common in the NO donor group. However, abdominal pain (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.44) and vaginal bleeding (RR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.27) were less frequent in the NO donor group. There was no significant difference in nausea or vomiting between the two groups (RR 1.17, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.46), and patient satisfaction was similar. One trial compared NO donors alone to a combination of NO donors and prostaglandins. The cumulative force required to dilate the cervix to 8 mm was higher in the NO donor group (mean difference 14.50, 95% CI 0.50 to 28.50). There were no significant differences in headache (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.38 to 2.00), abdominal pain (RR 0.14, 95% CI 0.02 to 1.07), or intraoperative blood loss (mean difference -50 mL, 95% CI -164.19 to 64.19) between the two groups. In conclusion, NO donors are more effective than placebo or no treatment for cervical ripening in first-trimester surgical abortion. However, they are less effective than prostaglandins and are associated with a higher incidence of side effects.
